content.overview: Legal scholarship commonly groups Directive Principles into socialistic, Gandhian, and liberal-intellectual categories for teaching and analysis. These labels are classificatory tools used in constitutional commentary; they are not themselves constitutional text and do not alter Article 37.

sections.heading: Socialistic principles (illustrative grouping)
sections.body: Principles aimed at social and economic justice and reducing inequality — for example the policy goals reflected in Articles 38, 39, 39A, 41, 42, 43, 43A and 47. Grouping is pedagogical; each Article has its own text.

sections.heading: Gandhian principles (illustrative grouping)
sections.body: Principles associated with village organisation, cottage industry, weaker sections, and related goals — often linked in teaching materials to Articles 40, 43, 46, 47 and 48. Always return to the official Article text.

sections.heading: Liberal-intellectual principles (illustrative grouping)
sections.body: Principles associated with uniform civil code, early childhood care and education, separation of judiciary and executive, and international peace — often linked in teaching to Articles 44, 45, 50 and 51.

sections.heading: Warning
sections.body: Do not plead a classification as if it were enacted law. Plead the Article, the implementing statute, and the Part III standard if rights are claimed.
